title: A uniform principal localization kills the generic torsion kernel
statement: Let A and B be commutative rings with B an A-algebra. Let K be a field with an A-algebra structure, K' a field with compatible K- and A-algebra structures, r a natural number, and L_j fields with K'-algebra structures for j in Fin(r). Fix a K'-algebra equivalence e from the quotient of (K tensor_A B) tensor_K K' by its nilradical onto the product of the L_j. Here the nilradical is the ideal of nilpotent elements. Assume B is a finite A-module [pqf-lem-finite-integral-lft] and K a fraction field of A. Let R0 be a Noetherian domain with compatible maps A to R0 to K' making K' a fraction field of R0. There exists nonzero t in R0 such that, for every s divisible by t and every principal localization R=R0[1/s] in the universe of A, with compatible maps A to R0 to R to K' and K' a fraction field of R, and every compatible R-algebra structure on the L_j, every R-algebra homomorphism f from (B tensor_A R) modulo its nilradical to the product of the L_j is injective if it is compatible. Call f compatible when for every b in B its value on the class of b tensor 1 is e of the class of (1 tensor b) tensor 1.

proof.text: Put C = (B tensor_A R0)_red. It is a finite R0-module. Tensor associativity identifies its generic localization with the source of e: reduction commutes with localization, since a fraction is nilpotent if and only if a denominator multiple of its numerator is nilpotent. The kernel of the map from C to its generic localization is torsion and finitely generated, since R0 is Noetherian. Choose a nonzero annihilator for each generator and take their product t (1 for no generators). Localizing at any s divisible by t kills the kernel. Localization is exact, so the induced map from the localized C to the generic product is injective. Reduction commutes with this principal localization and identifies its source with (B tensor_A R)_red. The pure-tensor compatibility determines the map f uniquely: R-linearity determines all pure tensors and additivity determines their sums; the quotient map is surjective. Thus f is the injective induced map. When the generic product is zero, the kernel is all of C and the same torsion argument kills C.
